perspective:
Keith has access to the following:

- Keith knows Elizabeth as the receptionist at the construction company where he works as a construction worker. They have a friendly but professional relationship and interact when he comes into the office for paperwork or project updates.
- Over the past few days, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt/short with him. He wondered whether he had unknowingly upset her or caused a misunderstanding.
- Keith asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, that she was just dealing with personal stuff, and she apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and wanted to support her. He told Elizabeth he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break. He heard her accept and thank him.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses, which Keith perceived as quite severe. Keith suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help. Elizabeth replied that she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- After that conversation, Keith noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn. He believed he might have embarrassed her by suggesting professional help and felt regretful. He apologized for possibly overstepping and told her he was there to support her. Elizabeth said he did not overstep, that she appreciated his concern, and that it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believes she values his support and feels more comfortable around him now. He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available to chat or take a break. Elizabeth thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.
